Bhattg is a much more experienced player than me and if I can win against him then you know how lol. ---

At this point I was thinking that maybe I was actually going to win again lol.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWxQQ6egnmV4m2dwx6YccPeqpDTHsbbF5J5jkuCRCL4Zb/1792605583911.jpg)

Thankfully my team managed to defeat his last monster and I won the battle!

This was honestly a really fun match because it's been quite a long time since I last played against bhattg.

result.body: One thing I find interesting about Splinterlands is how certain abilities can completely change the way I approach a battle. Recently, I have been paying more attention to abilities that provide support rather than dealing direct damage. One ability that deserves attention is Repair, especially when building a team that depends on armour to survive enemy attacks. A card I find interesting for this strategy is Scavo Hireling. Its Repair ability restores some armour to a friendly monster whose armour has taken damage. This can be useful when my lineup includes monsters that rely on armour to withstand attacks. Instead of allowing that armour to disappear completely, I can potentially restore some of it and make the frontline harder to break through. What I like about this strategy is that it encourages me to think beyond attack power. A monster that restores armour might not deal much damage itself, but its contribution can help another monster survive for longer. If my frontline remains standing, my attackers have more opportunities to weaken the opposing team. However, Repair is not equally useful in every battle. If my team has little or no armour, I may not get much value from the ability. This means I need to examine my other cards before deciding whether Scavo Hireling deserves a position in the lineup. Choosing a support monster without considering the rest of the team can waste valuable mana. I also need to think about the type of attacks my opponent is using. Armour can help against physical attacks, but magic attacks generally bypass armour unless specific abilities or rules change how the damage works. If the opposing team relies heavily on magic, an armour-focused strategy may not provide the protection I expect. This is why I find it important to read the battle rules before choosing my cards. Some rulesets can make armour more valuable, while others may encourage a completely different approach. Understanding these conditions helps me decide whether Repair is worth including or whether I should use a monster with a more suitable ability. Mana management is another challenge. Every support card takes up space in my lineup and may reduce the amount of mana available for attackers. If I include Scavo Hireling, I need to make sure I still have enough offensive power to defeat the enemy. A team that focuses entirely on staying alive can struggle if it cannot deal enough damage. Positioning also matters. I want my support monsters to remain alive long enough to use their abilities, especially when their contribution is important to the entire strategy. At the same time, I must consider whether the opponent has Sneak or other abilities that could threaten my backline. I think this is one of the most interesting aspects of building a team. Every card should have a purpose, and sometimes that purpose is not immediately obvious from its attack or health statistics. A support monster can become valuable because of how it improves the performance of another card. Going forward, I want to pay more attention to the relationship between armour, healing and other defensive abilities. They are not interchangeable, and each works differently depending on the battle conditions. Learning when to use them can help me avoid building a team that looks strong but has weaknesses I have overlooked. For me, Splinterlands is not only about finding powerful monsters. It is also about understanding how individual abilities work together. Hey everyone! Hope you are all doing well and enjoying your battles today.

Today I want to take a look at a Common Fire monster called **Emberscale Invoker**. This is a 7-mana Drakoshan card that brings magic damage and starts with the **Snipe** ability right from level 1. Since magic attacks ignore enemy armor, putting Snipe on a magic card lets you deal direct health damage to the opponent's backline attackers.

Let’s go through its stats, abilities, and how to place it properly in your Fire lineups!

---


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQYhP97bZ1Wi1498UQfCF7q8VvBJ7pcne8TMU5Rm64wkQ/1792588646142.jpg)

---

## Card Stats and Level Breakdown

Emberscale Invoker is built to sit in your middle positions, picking off squishy backline targets while providing armor repair as it levels up.

Here is how its stats grow across the levels:

* **Level 1 to 2:** Starts with 1 magic attack (jumps to 2 magic at level 2), 3 speed, 2 armor, and 5 health. It comes with **Snipe** right at level 1.
* **Level 3 to 4:** Magic attack stays at 2, speed stays at 3, armor moves up to 3, and health stays at 5. At level 3, it unlocks **Repair**.
* **Level 5 to 7:** Magic attack stays at 2, speed increases to 4, armor reaches 3 to 4, and health stays at 5. At level 5, it unlocks **Amplify**.
* **Level 8 to 10 (Max Level):** At level 8, magic attack reaches 3. By level 10 (max level), it reaches 3 magic attack, 4 speed, 4 armor, and 6 health while unlocking its fourth ability (**Silence**).

---


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaizsiWSWrAkVAAZ4fG4YPBphiFiwDPD3Dx3di9Dv2raJ/1792588664678.jpg)


---

## Understanding its Abilities

This card starts as a backline sniper and turns into a great support card as you level it up:


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaeRrHPuVJF2oR6PxAKnJB5KL7dRppDmq18WdDRuzBhok/1792588711437.png)


1. **Snipe** (Level 1): Targets enemy magic, ranged, or no-attack monsters instead of the main front tank.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmc8wwXvaxsHHkpAKB1E3fpRzNWiHacWXbjPGB5bqvrLrM/1792588720162.png)

2. **Repair** (Level 3): Restores a portion of the armor on whichever friendly monster has taken the most armor damage each round.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUGaZpFpcbuWTECBypkEDkAPAwE4RnpPhSkv8azxGXegF/1792588727723.png)

3. **Amplify** (Level 5): Increases the damage done by return abilities like Magic Reflect, Return Fire, and Thorns.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSJAzTFtyWSVJnpbfMSBdwtoxjqy9zPhjyN41cj5QkDkK/1792588737392.png)

4. **Silence** (Level 10): Reduces the magic attack power of all enemy monsters by -1.

Combining **Magic Attack + Snipe** right from level 1 is the main highlight here. Most backline ranged or magic monsters have low health and no Void armor, so hitting them directly with magic takes them out fast.

---

## How to Set It Up on the Battlefield

Because Emberscale Invoker is a magic attacker with 2 armor and 5 health, its best spot is **in the middle of your team** (Positions 2, 3, or 4).

Here is why this placement works:
- Keeping it protected behind your main tank allows it to fire Snipe shots safely every single turn.
- Once you reach level 3, placing it in the middle lets its **Repair** ability fix up your frontline tank's armor round after round.
- It works best in **Medium to High Mana matches** (28+ mana) where you have enough points for a heavy tank in slot 1 and extra attackers around it.

---

## Final Thoughts

Emberscale Invoker is a very handy utility card for Fire. Getting a magic sniper at level 1 helps you bypass annoying, heavily armored tanks and take down the opponent's main damage dealers first.

Have you tried using Emberscale Invoker in your Fire lineups yet? Do you use it mainly for Snipe damage or for the Repair support? Let me know in the comments below!

***Thanks for stopping by to read my post. See you all on the battlefield!***

Good morning, Summoners! This is @zusi78.

Before the new season started I deliberately brought in low-mana splinters built around Weapons Training. With their cheap costs they let me stay competitive in the very low-to-mid mana brackets where every point of mana is precious and the meta punishes bloated lineups. I’m enjoying that decision more than I expected—especially after wins like the one in the screenshot (Modern Ranked Bracket III).![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmY1RYsb6ZoGrZsKAubM3Vhx8RJwkFrsmjPF6yQCAm1TMV/1792576892323.jpg)


Big legendaries like **Rage** that has weapon training ability are great when the mana allows, but when the cap sits at 20–30 the player who can turn 2- and 3-mana utilities into attackers—while still fielding enough bodies—often comes out ahead.

That’s exactly where **Lucky Longshot** shines. It brings its own reliable pressure while still handing attack to the no-attack pieces next to it. The mana cost is friendly, the footprint is light, and you still get to fill the rest of the board with the cheap utilities that make low-mana lineups work. In short: **Rage** is fine when the mana allows, but **Lucky Longshot** is the tool that actually lets me feature more units when the cap is low.

On a separate note, huge thanks to @culebro for the reward from the “High Five or Four’s a Crowd” contest. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZYBxhXajnrhJeNH38xNjDjUEystRq334QPHnFX2ai86y/1792577725649.jpg)Participating earned me a Vaelok unit—the Rare Dragon from the Arena Vanguard set. Flying, Demoralize, and later Life Leech at full max make him a solid addition to the collection, and it was a nice bonus on top of the battle wins.
**Splinterlands is no walk in the park,but that's what amps up the excitement.A winning strategy weighs stas, abilities, rulesets, mana caps, and beyond. That's why you must factor them all into your deck building.Toss in strong cards to boost your setups, and push hard to rack up as many victories as possible**! 🔥.![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfSPs7mdQTibbmM14FAFzfH3G8oSxj9S92L9K6qezy6GQ/1779996340539.jpg)
**Weapons Training** is one of the cleanest and most flexible abilities in the game right now. Official description: it gives its attack type and power to adjacent no-attack units (maximum of 3 power). The training persists even after the trainer dies. You can place one trainee on each side of the trainer.




**My Core No-Attack Weapon-Training Targets This Season**.

**These two Rebellion-era commons form the backbone of the strategy**:

**Chaos Animator**(Death, 3 mana)![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmR9Ro8GMiMAU6WTZBz6ey6gmXVE2NFBGY9ufWgh4KuWvS/1792579013084.jpg)Amplify from level 1 (boosts Return Fire, Thorns, Magic Reflect, etc.), Void at higher levels, and Redemption on death. Another pure support piece that becomes a dual-threat once Weapons Training lands. Pair it with any counter-damage cards and Amplify makes the reflect hits hurt a lot more.

**Ahna-Chei Botanist**(Death, 2 mana)![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmX7i7PMxBHTYarx4X7WzDA1JsuP9Tx61SQZaiVLpLWF85/1792579044270.jpg)Return Fire + Blind (and later Dispel). Classic low-mana disruptor. Blind makes enemy melee and ranged attacks miss more often; Return Fire punishes the ones that connect. Give it Weapons Training and it starts dealing its own damage while still disrupting. Extremely efficient in Little League or any under-20 mana ruleset.![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfSPs7mdQTibbmM14FAFzfH3G8oSxj9S92L9K6qezy6GQ/1779996340539.jpg)


**The Battle**![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNXKHtnzNEKEzLJAdNzw2kqSP3JoTa5uGhi8xp4Roz5pJ/1792580247899.jpg)In this battle the total mana cap is 26 and you are to choose splinters from Fire,Water, Earth,Life and Death elements.And the ruleset is no modifier.



In this battle the key formation was simple and effective:
Chaos Animator (left trainee) + Lucky Longshot (trainer) + Ahna-Chei Botanist (right trainee)
Two non-attackers flanking the Lucky Longshot. That positioning granted the trainees 1 ranged attack and 1 magic attack. Suddenly the pure utility pieces were contributing dual-type damage while still performing their original support roles. Because the training persists, even if Lucky Longshot went down the newly armed monsters kept applying pressure from both attack types.![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdLFgMuVzSSWACcT6matjU2DBP5BSM8cwvPcung7sSe3h/1792580779503.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQjpLFceMX6a48AEFDDTbUAQtm8Apw3h9WPJQjSQCjLxK/1792580779560.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWhgPKsKgacqhj1hitd1N9kDLnQHoEBVDJvydbU5n5A8o/1792580779609.jpg)[Watch the replay](https://splinterlands.com/battle/sl_5b3acb943da0e656934a995ee2edefc7?ref=zusi78)![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfSPs7mdQTibbmM14FAFzfH3G8oSxj9S92L9K6qezy6GQ/1779996340539.jpg)

Splinterlands is a fun game.If you haven’t joined yet, here’s my referral link to participate:
[Join here](https://splinterlands.com/?ref=zusi78)

Thank you for reading and watching my post. @zusi78 signing off.

As my Glint earnings have increased, I have also ramped up my purchases of card packs. As you know, reaching higher levels requires an increasing number of copies of a card; therefore, it is essential to purchase as many packs as possible—or acquire cards through other means—to expand your deck. Once a new card set is launched, the current set may be removed from the reward system, leaving direct purchase as the only way to obtain these cards. This is why I am consistently adding new cards to my deck. Although these cards are "soulbound"—meaning they cannot be traded—I can use them in my gameplay for as long as I like. Furthermore, I have the option to purchase scrolls to "unbind" them. For now, however, I am simply collecting cards; once I have had the chance to use them across various battle conditions, I will choose to unbind only those that I find most effective or enjoyable.

Today, I upgraded two rare cards to level 3. One of these—a Fire-element melee attack card called 'Grove Doomblade'—recently earned a spot among my favorite cards; it is well-known for its massive melee attack power. I wasn't particularly fond of this card at level 1, but at level 2, it gained the 'Fury' ability. This ability doubles its attack power against enemies possessing the 'Taunt' trait—meaning that if it faces a card with 'Taunt,' its 5 melee attack power effectively becomes 10, which is enough to knock out almost any card in a single strike. Ever since it reached level 2, it has been one of my favorites, and now, at level 3, it has gained an additional +1 Health, further strengthening it. I typically use this card in combination with the 'Double Strike' ability—and occasionally the 'Swiftness' ability—resulting in an truly impressive performance on the battlefield.

The second rare card is the Earth-element magic attack card, 'Anchor-Hex Adept.' This card joined my list of favorites starting at Level 2, as that is when it gained the 'Divine Shield' ability—a feature that allows it to ignore one instance of incoming damage. While ignoring a single hit might seem minor, it can have a significant impact on the battlefield; consequently, I began using this card much more frequently from Level 2 onwards, and its performance was consistently praiseworthy. At Level 3, it receives an upgrade of +1 armor, which further strengthens it. Although this armor offers no protection against magic-based attacks, opponents relying on melee or ranged attacks must break through it before they can reach the card's health, making it even more resilient than before. By positioning it somewhere in the middle of your lineup, you can rest easy—at least as far as this card is concerned.

* * *

Splinterlands isn't an easy place, but that's what makes it even more fun. A perfect strategy takes into account many factors, including stats, abilities, rulesets, mana caps, and more. That's why it's even more important to consider all these factors when developing a strategy. Add good cards to your deck, but also work on improving your strategies, and strive to win as many battles as possible!🔥

If you also want to enjoy this amazing game and you have not yet signed up, I invite you to Splinterlands, and I will also try my best to guide you in this game. 😎

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmP33oTbPrM9bC72pr9e9c6QNGS4MTcX6XWGcsCx9B1XyU/pasted_1792581544008.png)

One mechanic I find interesting in Splinterlands is the Blast ability. It adds another layer to attacking because the damage does not always stop at the monster being targeted. When used effectively, Blast can also damage monsters adjacent to the target, allowing a single attack to put pressure on multiple enemies.

One card I find worth exploring is Ruler of the Seas. This Water monster has magic attack and the Blast ability, making it an interesting option when I want to deal damage beyond a single target. I like the idea of using magic attacks to weaken an enemy formation while also taking advantage of the additional damage from Blast.

What makes this ability interesting is how much positioning matters. If the enemy team has several monsters standing next to one another, Blast can create opportunities to damage more than one monster during an attack. This means I need to pay attention to the opposing formation rather than focusing only on the monster in the first position.

However, Blast is not automatically effective in every battle. If the target has no adjacent monsters, there may be fewer opportunities to benefit from the additional damage. I also need to consider whether my chosen attacker can survive long enough to contribute. A powerful monster is less useful if it gets eliminated before it has the chance to attack.

Another important factor is the mana cap. Some monsters with useful abilities can be expensive, and including one may force me to make sacrifices elsewhere. If I choose a strong Blast attacker, I still need a frontline monster that can absorb attacks and other cards that help maintain the team’s balance.

I have also been thinking about how magic damage fits into this strategy. Magic attackers can be useful because their attacks generally bypass armour, although abilities such as Void and certain rulesets can change how effective they are. Combining magic damage with Blast can create pressure, but I should always consider whether the opponent has a way to reduce or counter those attacks.

The ruleset is another part of the decision. Before building my team, I want to check whether the battle conditions support my preferred strategy. Some rules may encourage different types of attacks or change the value of particular monsters. Adapting to these conditions is better than choosing the same lineup without considering what the battle requires.

Positioning my own monsters matters just as much. While I am looking for opportunities to damage several enemies, I also need to protect my important attackers. If my frontline falls too quickly, the rest of the team may become vulnerable before I can take advantage of its abilities.

What I appreciate about Blast is that it encourages me to think about the overall formation instead of looking at individual cards in isolation. The value of a monster depends not only on its attack but also on how its abilities interact with the enemy team.

I want to keep exploring different combinations and learn when Blast provides the most value. Sometimes, a card that deals damage to several targets can create an advantage that a single-target attacker cannot provide as easily. The challenge is recognising the right situation and building a team that supports the strategy.

For me, that is part of the enjoyment of Splinterlands. There are many abilities to understand, different lineups to experiment with and plenty of ways to approach a battle. The more attention I pay to these details, the more thoughtful my decisions become.

<center>https://img.leopedia.io/DQmduG7rk91KygpkYscCFbE2ztRWE58rVfyHHeXqHzy7fC6/Portada%20-%20Equalized%20Armor.png</center>

<center>Yesterday, with the game update on [**2026-10-20**](https://docs.splinterlands.com/platform/release-notes/2026#id-2026-10-20), the **Splinterlands** team brought us another new Ruleset that can drastically alter the tempo and duration of battles, making them much more defensive. This new Ruleset is:</center>

><center>El día de ayer, con la actualización del [**2026-10-20**](https://docs.splinterlands.com/platform/release-notes/2026#id-2026-10-20), el equipo de **Splinterlands** nos trae otra nueva Ruleset que puede cambiar bastante el ritmo y la duración de las batallas haciéndolas más defensivas, y esa Ruleset nueva es:</center>

## <center>Equalized Armor</center>
<center>https://img.leopedia.io/DQmNT9SH7qNRdG6ZeKF3s7DjANFELstRc3aa1GmdE2fpG76/img_combat-rule_equalized-armor_150.png</center>

- **Equalized Armor:** The Initial Armor of all Units is equal to that of the Unit on either team with the highest base Armor.

>- **Equalized Armor:** La armadura inicial de cada unidad es igual a la de la unidad de cualquiera de los dos equipos con la mayor armadura base.

<center>https://img.leopedia.io/DQmY5KpTtvoAAcdA1MQGHRcntUSwoGjyyxXLCVtpYnLQ4wz/image.png</center>

<center>In simple terms, every unit's starting armor on the field will match the highest base armor value present among all fielded cards across both teams. While at first glance it appears to be the physical protection equivalent of the classic **Equalizer** a mechanic that traditionally equalizes health pools the arrival of **Equalized Armor** will make matches lean much more defensive in most cases, extending round counts and elevating the value of skills that previously saw situational usage.</center>

><center>En términos sencillos, la armadura inicial de cada unidad en el campo se igualará a la cantidad base de armadura que posea la carta con el valor más alto entre ambos equipos. Y aunque a primera vista parece ser la versión orientada a la protección física de la clásica **Equalizer** una mecánica que tradicionalmente empareja los puntos de salud con la llegada de **Equalized Armor** las batallas tomarán una tónica mucho más defensiva en la mayoría de los casos, extendiendo el número de rondas e impulsando el valor de habilidades que antes tenían un uso condicionado.</center>

### <center>Redefining unit value: The rise of support and high-armor tanks | Redefiniendo el valor de las unidades: El auge del soporte y tanques de alto blindaje</center>

<center>The immediate impact of this battle condition will be noticed during monster selection in the lineup phase. To maximize the benefit of **Equalized Armor**, it will become almost mandatory to include at least **1** unit with an extremely high base armor value, ensuring our entire team receives a colossal initial shield.</center>

><center>El impacto inmediato de esta condición de batalla se notará en la selección de monstruos durante la fase de alineación. Para sacar el máximo provecho de **Equalized Armor**, se volverá casi obligatorio incluir al menos **1** unidad que posea un valor de armadura extremadamente elevado, garantizando que todo nuestro equipo reciba un escudo inicial colosal.</center>

<center>In this scenario, low mana cost cards with massive armor transform into top-priority support engines. A perfect example is **Clockwork Aide**, a unit that, thanks to its high defensive ratio relative to its mana cost, can be deployed as a passive driver solely to inject that huge shield amount into all allied units. Likewise, cards with overwhelming natural armor will gain huge meta presence over options that, despite appearing stronger individually in attack power or speed, fail to provide that global defensive boost.</center>

><center>En este escenario, cartas de bajo costo de maná pero con blindaje masivo pasan a convertirse en piezas de soporte prioritarias. Un ejemplo perfecto de esto es **Clockwork Aide**, una unidad que, gracias a su alto valor defensivo en relación con su costo, puede ser desplegada como un motor pasivo únicamente para inyectar esa enorme cantidad de armadura a todo el equipo aliado. Asimismo, cartas con armaduras naturales abrumadoras ganarán muchísima presencia en el metajuego sobre otras opciones que, aunque individualmente puedan parecer más fuertes en ataque o velocidad, no aportan ese impulso defensivo global.</center>

### <center>The battle against the shield: Corrosive Ward, Rust, Piercing, and magic damage | La batalla contra el escudo: Corrosive Ward, Rust, Piercing y daño mágico</center>

<center>When facing battles where every opposing unit can start with **8**, **10**, or more armor points, relying exclusively on conventional physical damage becomes a headache. For this reason, **Equalized Armor** will force players to dust off and integrate defensive disruption tools on a massive scale.</center>

><center>Al enfrentarnos a batallas donde cada unidad en la alineación enemiga puede iniciar con **8**, **10** o más puntos de armadura, depender exclusivamente del daño físico convencional se convertirá en un dolor de cabeza. Por esta razón, **Equalized Armor** obligará a los jugadores a desempolvar e integrar masivamente herramientas de disrupción defensiva.</center>

<center>Abilities like **Rust** (to reduce enemy team armor), **Corrosive Ward**, and **Piercing** will see a drastic spike in usage. Meanwhile, fielding magic-based compositions will stand out as one of the most popular and efficient counters, since magic attacks completely bypass shields to strike enemy health bars directly.</center>

><center>Habilidades como **Rust** (para reducir la armadura global del rival), **Corrosive Ward** y **Piercing** verán un incremento drástico en su tasa de uso. Por su parte, la inclusión de alineaciones basadas en daño mágico será una de las respuestas más populares y eficientes, ya que el ataque mágico permite sobrepasar por completo el escudo para impactar directamente en la barra de salud de los enemigos.</center>

### <center>The decisive role of Shatter | El papel determinante de Shatter</center>

<center>Among the mechanical answers to counter this rule, units or Archons featuring **Shatter** will position themselves as true strategic gems. **Shatter** holds the power to instantly obliterate a target's entire armor pool upon landing a single hit, nullifying the rule's benefit on that unit in a single instant.</center>

><center>Dentro de las respuestas mecánicas para contrarrestar esta regla, las unidades u Archons que cuenten con la habilidad **Shatter** se posicionarán como verdaderas joyas de estrategia. **Shatter** posee la capacidad de destruir instantáneamente toda la armadura del objetivo tras asestar un solo golpe, anulando en un instante el beneficio que la regla le otorgó a esa unidad.</center>

<center>As a player who loves competing with **Immortalis**, this rule is immensely attractive and exciting. **Immortalis** is one of the few Archons granting **Shatter** to all allied units, dismantling colossal enemy defenses in early combat rounds while pairing it with magic damage reduction to neutralize opponents attempting to bypass armor through magic.</center>

><center>Como jugador al que le encanta competir con **Immortalis**, esta regla resulta sumamente atractiva y emocionante. **Immortalis** es uno de los pocos Archons que otorga la habilidad **Shatter** a sus unidades, lo que permite desarmar defensas enemigas colosales en las primeras rondas del combate, combinándolo además con su reducción de daño mágico para neutralizar a los rivales que intenten atacarnos por esa vía.</center>

### <center>Explosive combos with Armor Strike | Combos explosivos con Armor Strike</center>

<center>Another ability heavily impacted by this new condition is **Armor Strike**. This mechanic enables a unit to execute an extra attack whose power scales off the remaining armor it holds at that moment.</center>

><center>Otra de las habilidades que se verá fuertemente impactada por esta nueva condición es **Armor Strike**. Esta mecánica permite a una unidad ejecutar un ataque adicional cuyo poder depende de la cantidad de armadura que conserve en ese momento.</center>

<center>Under **Equalized Armor**, we will witness striking and chaotic battle moments: low-attack units receiving a massive starting armor boost can hit with devastating force through **Armor Strike**, taking down core tanks or key pieces in **1** hit like a nuclear bomb. These rare, unexpected synergies will generate highly enjoyable and memorable combat highlights.</center>

><center>Bajo la influencia de **Equalized Armor**, podremos presenciar momentos verdaderamente llamativos y caóticos en la batalla: unidades de bajo ataque que, al recibir un impulso de armadura descomunal al inicio de la partida, podrán golpear con una potencia devastadora a través de **Armor Strike**, siendo capaces de eliminar a tanques o unidades clave de un solo golpe como una bomba nuclear. Se crearán momentos sumamente divertidos y llamativos en las batallas gracias a estos combos raros e inesperados.</center>

### <center>Conclusion </center>

<center>In general terms, **Equalized Armor** may not be immediately labeled as one of the most flashy or chaotic Rulesets, as its primary effect in most matchups simply extends battle length by adding a couple of attrition rounds. However, in the hands of players who read synergies like **Shatter**, **Armor Strike**, or the smart use of Archons like **Immortalis**, this new condition turns into fertile ground for tactical calculations and highly destructive strategies.</center>

><center>En líneas generales, **Equalized Armor** tal vez no sea calificada de entrada como una de las Rulesets más vistosas o caóticas del juego, ya que su efecto primario en la mayoría de los enfrentamientos será simplemente extender la duración de la batalla sumando un par de rounds adicionales de desgaste. No obstante, en manos de jugadores que sepan leer las sinergias de habilidades como **Shatter**, **Armor Strike** o el uso inteligente de Archons como **Immortalis**, esta nueva condición se transformará en un terreno fértil para el cálculo táctico y la creación de estrategias altamente destructivas.</center>

# RULESET 1: FEROCITY

This is a ruleset where all units have Fury ability. And what does this Ferocity ruleset do? It deals double damage to any target that possesses the Taunt ability.

Because of this Ferocity ability relying on Taunt units becomes extremely risky because opposing attackers will strike them with double power.

According to this ruleset it is necessary to adopt a strategy where you avoid using Taunt cards or prepare heavy defense for the battle.

## RULESET 2: REVERSE SPEED

This is a ruleset where units with the lowest speed attack first and have the highest chance to evade attacks. 

And what does this Reverse Speed ruleset do? It completely flips the standard speed order making slower units act first on the turn order.

Normally it happens that higher speed will attach first but according to this ruleset the situation is reversed.


Because of this Reverse Speed ability bringing cards with high speed stat actually becomes a disadvantage because they will take their turns last.

According to this ruleset it is necessary to adopt a strategy where you pick slow heavy hitters with 1 or 2 speed so they can strike before the opponent.

## RULESET 3: BROKEN ARROWS

This is a ruleset where you cannot summon units with ranged attacks. And what does this Broken Arrows ruleset do? It disables all ranged damage dealers from being selected.

Because of this Broken Arrows ability both players are forced to rely purely on melee and magic units.

According to this ruleset it is necessary to adopt a strategy where you build a strong lineup around melee front liners and magic attackers.

![Screenshot 2026-10-21 104311.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aliakbar2/23u5vMvh24tWcXauZUeA4kVhBzMxwfA1cPax1WcwjRDhMRRv11xzRMSBPazc1Y7Hkhi3J.png)


## MY STRATEGY AND MONSTERS SELECTION

Keeping these three rulesets in mind what strategy did I adopt and which units did I select? I knew that under Broken Arrows I needed a mix of melee and magic and under Reverse Speed I needed slow units.

First of all I selected my Archon Marlai Singariel which gives +1 magic to my allied units. In normal battles this speed boost is very good but under Reverse Speed granting extra speed accidentally made my units slower in turn order.

On the front line in first position I selected my main front tank with high health and armor to take heavy hits.

In the second position I selected my second melee unit with reach ability with 2 speed to provide early attacks.

In the third position I selected my third melee card to add extra physical attack power. And also that have magic attack power where it continues to attack being at 3rd position.

The 4th and 5th position monsters were the mix of magic attackers that will continue to perform +2 magic attacks every round.

In the sixth position I selected my backline support card which has return ability as well.


![Screenshot 2026-10-21 104440.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aliakbar2/23tvkkQ6KuQLSVgutxpb1x9tYgAcuubj7afQTCHHtP977fyvJTxFYBcSqQdy2WKnDaMV2.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-21 104416.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aliakbar2/23tmKiezZjcS4fURfg4o3WQhj8jLpbaU4NYtn2SqwUDy4LivgwCAgFj4ECNJLcULKJJDn.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-21 104410.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aliakbar2/23u65Px5Wq2m2fZR59pXFZHGjjNgDuUB4eNwSEUE8tnNQeg6Ep42efqQH1imfwnnPu2dE.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-21 104403.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aliakbar2/23uQpSEJWcXxnGHZQcpuNr4V8TxBncDHWracu4pNwxGp6KD8imAJckiHKcjQstg7KFZCP.png)

## ON THE BATTLEFIELD

When I looked at the enemy lineup on the battlefield it was also quite interesting. They had brought a team that utilized slow units very well under Reverse Speed including a slow front tank with 2 speed.

The battle started with initial strikes coming from both sides. Heavy attacks continued till first round.

In Round 1 both sides traded hits. The enemy's slower units took advantage of Reverse Speed and attacked first taking down my front line defenses before my team could launch their full power.

In Round 2 the enemy pushed their advantage further. Their front line units dealt continuous damage and eliminated my main tank leaving my middle cards exposed.

In round 2, the battle was 5vs4 which was still interesting. But as round 3 started I realized that I have lost this battle.

In Round 3 the battle came to an end. My remaining magic unit tried to hold the position but the enemy's combined forces were too strong.

![Screenshot 2026-10-21 104346.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aliakbar2/23tRvMsc64yrcsCsbS2EpdUBqwc87zx98vaFVUHyGg9BX2tZ1bd58HXssn558fhViK3qk.png)


At the end of Round 3 I faced a defeat. The main reason was that I didnot understand the rulesets properly and I had wrong monster selections in the end.


What would your strategy be in this type of ruleset and which units would you give more preference to? Will be glad to see your answers in the comment section.

I hope you find this post useful and informative.. If you do, please remember to reblog it so that it reaches as many people as possible and that they can benefit the most from it. Also remember to upvote which will help me financially and grow my account.
